subject: Retention & Erasure: AzureSettle delegated log deletion + SIG/CAIQ evidence
messages:
From: Elena Park <security@azuresettle.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: AzureSettle Compliance Team <compliance@azuresettle.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Question: tenant-scoped deletion path + SIG/CAIQ evidence

Hi Rafael,

Thanks for taking this. We're in the middle of our SIG/CAIQ review and a few specifics popped up around tenant-scoped log retention that I wanted to put on your radar. Our default requirement for tenant debug logs is 90 days; I see Redwood's standard session/log TTL is 30 days.

We have two asks (high level):
- Can you describe the customer-specific deletion override path? We need a clear chain of control showing who can request/approve an exception and an auditable deletion execution (API call/job id, timestamps).
- Evidence: For any exception you provide, we need artifacts suitable for SIG/CAIQ and our security team: retention matrix (showing system-level default vs tenant override), deletion playbook (steps & runbook), an example proof-of-delete artifact for one tenant (audit log + job id + export showing zeroed data).

I've attached our questionnaire and a short worksheet to map your answers (Azuresettle_SIG_Questions_20260914.xlsx). Can we align on a deliverable timeline? We are trying to close this week but can accept a staged delivery: (a) retention matrix + playbook draft, (b) proof-of-delete example, (c) a signed attestation if available.

Also, one technical question for your infra/security engineer: do you run any long-lived KV caches or debugging traces outside core session logs that would require separate deletion flows?

Best,
Elena Park
Security & Compliance
AzureSettle

[Attachment: Azuresettle_SIG_Questions_20260914.xlsx (xlsx)]

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
To: Elena Park <security@azuresettle.com>
Cc: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Sep 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Question: tenant-scoped deletion path + SIG/CAIQ evidence

Elena — thanks for the clear ask and the worksheet. Apologies for the short turnaround on timing; we can do a staged delivery as you suggested.

Short answers up front:
- Delegated exceptions: we support tenant-scoped retention overrides via an internal workflow (Customer Exception Request). Approval requires a CS request + Security signoff + Product ops recorded in our ticketing system. The deletion itself is executed by our secure erase job and recorded in the audit log with a job id and granular timestamps.
- Evidence: we will provide (1) a retention matrix mapping system default vs tenant overrides, (2) our deletion & evidence playbook (how the secure erase job works and where artifacts live), and (3) one proof-of-delete sample for a sandbox tenant.

I've uploaded a draft retention matrix and an initial checklist to a shared drive and attached the draft matrix to this thread: Redwood-Retention-Matrix-draft-20260914.xlsx. Jasmine, can you coordinate the customer-oriented language & delivery schedule for AzureSettle?

Sooj in (cc) — can you confirm whether KV-caches or model inference traces need separate erasure flows (Elena's technical question below). If so, please add the suggested artifacts we can include in the evidence packet.

Proposed timeline (staged):
1) By EOD Tue 2026-09-15: retention matrix + deletion playbook draft + links to runbook artifacts.
2) By Thu 2026-09-17: one proof-of-delete sample (sandbox tenant) and a draft SIG/CAIQ response PDF.
3) If needed, a signed attestation the following week (DocuSign).

If that works I'll schedule a short 30-min call to walk the packet on Wed morning.

Thanks,
Rafael Mendes
Director, Compliance Solutions
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: Redwood-Retention-Matrix-draft-20260914.xlsx (xlsx)]

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>, Elena Park <security@azuresettle.com>
Cc: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 08:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Question: tenant-scoped deletion path + SIG/CAIQ evidence

Thanks Rafael. Quick technical breakdown to help AZ-settle's compliance team: 

1) Surface of logs/data scopes:
- Session logs (default TTL 30 days) — central logging cluster managed by Redwood.
- Debug traces & model-inference tracebacks — stored in a segmented blob store; default TTL 30 days but we support tenant-level TTLs via metadata tags.
- KV caches / in-memory session KV — ephemeral; persisted snapshots for debugging only on demand and labeled with tenant ids and snapshot ids.

2) Deletion mechanism & evidence artifacts:
- Deletion is a two-step pipeline: (A) mark-for-deletion via the Customer Exception Request system (audit trail: ticket id, approver, timestamp), (B) secure erase job which uses the job id to target tenant-scoped objects (blob keys, index entries, snapshot ids).
- Proof-of-delete artifact we can produce: secure-erase-job.log (contains job id, start/end timestamps, number of objects targeted, checksum of record set before/after), audit-log-entry (ticket id, approver), and a one-line summary csv enumerating deleted object keys (for your SOC team to reconcile).
- For immutable snapshots or escrowed archives (rare), we run an offline purge and provide certificate of erasure from the storage subsystem.

3) Controls around keys and backups:
- KMS-backed object keys are rotated on schedule; deleted objects are zeroed and pointer metadata removed; we keep an index of deleted object ids for 90 days for forensic reconciliation only and then purge index entries. The index retention is itself auditable and part of the evidence artifact.

4) SIG/CAIQ specifics we will include in the draft: mapping of control IDs to artifacts, sample job log redactions, and a step-by-step runbook for the secure erase flow.

Attached is a working version of a SIG response PDF we can massage into customer format: SIG-Response-Draft-Sept2026.pdf. Rafael/Jasmine: I added technical appendix placeholders that we will need to fill after we run the sandbox deletion.

--
Soojin Lee
Security Engineer, Redwood Inference

[Attachment: SIG-Response-Draft-Sept2026.pdf (pdf)]

Subject: Re: Question: tenant-scoped deletion path + SIG/CAIQ evidence

Rafael / Soojin — this looks good, thanks. The staged timeline is fine. A few clarifying notes and one ask: 

- On evidence: the proof-of-delete artifact format you described (secure-erase-job.log + audit-log-entry + deleted-keys.csv) is exactly what our auditors expect. Please ensure sample logs have sensitive values redacted and a short readme describing how to verify the check-sums.
- For KV snapshots: we need confirmation in writing that snapshots labeled with tenant id will be included in the secure erase (even if stored in escrow for debugging). That confirmation can be a short paragraph in your playbook.
- For the attestation: we prefer a short DocuSign statement affirming Redwood executed the deletion and that artifacts are authentic. Can you draft a brief attestation paragraph we can route for signature?

Next steps I propose:
1) Your deliverable tomorrow: retention matrix + deletion playbook draft + link to the workspace folder.
2) By Thu EOD: proof-of-delete sample in the workspace (sandbox tenant). We will run this through a quick internal review.

If the sandbox evidence looks good we'll ask for the attestation to be DocuSigned.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Best,
Elena Park
Security & Compliance
AzureSettle
